title: composed unions in Mapped[] as used in new doc examples do not parse correctly with future annotations

labels.name: blocker
labels.description: issue that must be resolved asap as it is preventing things from working

labels.name: near-term release
labels.description: addition to the milestone which indicates this should be in a near-term release

labels.name: orm - annotated declarative
labels.description: issues with the new annotations-based declarative ORM approach

body:
I was concerned this was a regression introduced in a4e38d119913ca18462f2e9c6448c6e24d369df3 but this seems to have been there all along

you can work around this using newtype / type where the complex expression is not present in `Mapped[]`, but this is literally the example we have in the [new docs](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/declarative_tables.html#union-types-inside-the-type-map)

```py
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Union

from sqlalchemy.dialects import postgresql
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped
from sqlalchemy.orm import mapped_column
from sqlalchemy.schema import CreateTable

json_list_union = Union[list[int], list[str]]

class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    type_annotation_map = {
        json_list_union: postgresql.JSONB,
    }


class SomeClass(Base):
    __tablename__ = "some_table"

    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    list_col_pipe: Mapped[list[int] | list[str]]   # fails to parse
    list_col_union: Mapped[Union[list[int], list[str]]]  # fails to parse

print(CreateTable(SomeClass.__table__).compile(dialect=postgresql.dialect()))
```
